name: Minnesota
summary: Statutes, session laws, constitution, court rules, Minnesota Rules and the State Register are all on revisor.mn.gov, with clean per-section, per-rule and per-part URLs that both WebFetch and fetch_doc.py read (statutes and agency rules are UELMA-authenticated; the court-rule pages are disclaimed as unofficial). Case law is the gap: mncourts.gov shows only the current week's releases, its opinion PDFs are robots-disallowed and the shell gets a Cloudflare challenge; the State Law Library's static archive (1996 to Feb. 2016) is WebFetch-readable, while its 1996-present search is CAPTCHA-protected. Justia (tier 2) is the working route for opinion text, constructible by docket. Subsequent history: the Supreme Court keeps the Court of Appeals docket on review; denials are on the current PFR list or the 1996-2016 archive PFR PDFs, otherwise only in P-MACS (blocked).

examples: Thigpen v. Best Home Care LLC, No. A23-1544 (Minn. App. July 29, 2024)
State v. Senn, No. A25-1783 (Minn. App. Oct. 5, 2026)

citation_map.notes: No public-domain citation format: Minnesota cites N.W.2d / N.W.3d (Minn. reports ended at vol. 312, 1977, from memory). Minn. R. Civ. App. P. 136.01, subd. 1(c) (effective Aug. 1, 2020): nonprecedential opinions are not binding but may be cited as persuasive; older 'unpublished' opinions are governed by Minn. Stat. § 480A.08, subd. 3. Minnesota style uses 'Minn. App.' where Bluebook uses 'Minn. Ct. App.'; both are matched. The same appellate docket number (A##-####) is used in the Court of Appeals and, on review, in the Supreme Court (Thigpen, A23-1544, verified on Justia), so a docket finds the later Supreme Court decision. Pre-2000s dockets look like C3-96-1234. Route bare docket numbers (A25-1783) and WL cites here only with Minnesota context: 'A##-####' collides with other courts' docket styles. Bare 'Rule 12' or 'R. Civ. P.' without 'Minn.' must not route here. The prose form of the General Rules of Practice requires 'Minnesota' ('Rule 115 of the Minnesota General Rules of Practice'): the bare 'General Rules of Practice' also names North Carolina's 'General Rules of Practice for the Superior and District Courts' (build.py --cross). Constitution articles are matched in Roman or Arabic numerals ('art. 1, § 7'). 'Minn. R.' followed immediately by NNNN.NNNN is an administrative rule part (Minn. R. 7050.0222); 'Minn. R. Civ. P.', 'Minn. R. Evid.' etc. are court rules — the admin regex requires digits right after 'Minn. R.'. Statute sections are CHAPTER.SECTION (541.05, 260C.007, 3E.04); UCC sections carry a hyphen (336.2-725). A range 'Minn. Stat. §§ 609.185-.19' or '§§ 541.05-541.07' is a span: the regex keeps the first section and does not read the hyphen as part of the number (only '-digits' not followed by '.digit' is kept, as in 336.2-725). Revisor history notes use '2015 c 5 art 15 s 18' (session law) and '9 SR 2276' (State Register). 'SR' and 'Minn. Reg.' should only route here with Minnesota context. law_aliases map court-rule citation prefixes to the Revisor's court_rules path key used in mn-courtrules-revisor's url_pattern. CourtListener ids 'minn' and 'minnctapp' are from memory, unverified. Examples marked (form only) illustrate citation shape, not real cases; the WL branch of the docket pattern has no example (no real WL number was verified).

sources.title: Minnesota Statutes (Revisor of Statutes)
sources.publisher: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
sources.official_status_evidence: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/info: two official versions — the printed edition and the online authenticated PDFs designated under Minn. Stat. § 3E.04, subd. 2 (UELMA). HTML pages carry the footer 'Official Publication of the State of Minnesota' and an 'Authenticate' link; per-section PDF at /statutes/cite/{section}/pdf.
sources.coverage: Current edition (2025 Minnesota Statutes) per section; prior editions by year from the 1940s/1905 compilations onward (/statutes/{year}/cite/{section}); version lists per section; full chapter text at /statutes/cite/{chapter}/full.

access.pattern_rules: section verbatim as cited, chapter prefix included (541.05, 609.185, 336.2-725, 260C.007). No padding. Specific edition: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/{year}/cite/{section} (verified 2024 and 2025). Legacy form /statutes/?id={section} 301-redirects to /statutes/cite/{section}. Authenticated PDF: /statutes/cite/{section}/pdf. Chapter TOC: /statutes/cite/{chapter}; whole chapter: /statutes/cite/{chapter}/full (very long: ch. 609 = 1.06M chars). Subdivision anchors: /statutes/{year}/cite/{section}/subd/{section}.{n}.

automation.notes: Script is the primary route. Section pages are 8-11K chars of text (nav menu ~5.4K chars precedes the body), so WebFetch reads them whole. WebFetch on the bare built URL /statutes/cite/541.05 hit PROVENANCE_REQUIRED (permission prompt) — the search-surfaced form /statutes/2025/cite/609.185 and /statutes/?id=… went through. Repealed sections return a stub '[Repealed, …]', not body text.

currency.where: page heading above the section and in the right-hand resource box

hazards: Current edition is 2025: 2026 session-law amendments are not in the text until the 2026 edition; check /statutes/table2?full={section} (Statutes Changed, Table 2) and 'Recent History' on the page
repealed sections return a short repeal stub (e.g. 441.51 'MS 1984 [Repealed, 1984 c 543 s 69]')
full-chapter pages are huge (ch. 609 ≈ 1.06M chars) — use per-section pages
built URLs may need WebFetch approval; the script route is reliable

sources.title: Minnesota Court Rules (Revisor of Statutes, per rule)
sources.publisher: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes (rules promulgated by the Minnesota Supreme Court)
sources.official_status_evidence: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/court_rules/info/: 'Rules information on this website is not intended to replace an official source'; the official edition is the printed Minnesota Court Rules volume (Minn. Stat. § 3C.08).
sources.coverage: Civil Procedure (cp), Evidence (ev), Criminal Procedure (cr), General Rules of Practice (gp), Appellate Procedure (ap: subtypes rcap = Civil Appellate Procedure, spec = Special Rules of Practice for the Court of Appeals, flam = family/other), Juvenile (ju), District Court Special Rules (dc), Professional Rules (pr: cond = Rules of Professional Conduct, prof = Lawyers Professional Responsibility, judi, admi, boar …), Record Access (ra), Sentencing Guidelines (sg), Miscellaneous (ms).

access.pattern_rules: set/subtype key from citation_map.law_aliases: Minn. R. Civ. P. → cp; Minn. R. Evid. → ev; Minn. R. Crim. P. → cr; Minn. Gen. R. Prac. → gp; Minn. R. Civ. App. P. → ap/subtype/rcap; Minn. R. Prof. Conduct → pr/subtype/cond. {rule} = the whole rule number before the first dot for cp/cr/gp/rcap (12.02(e) → id/12; 15.01 → id/15; 115.03 → id/115; 103.03 → id/103), with the subpart anchored as #12.02; evidence rules are three/four digits (id/702); Professional Conduct uses the dotted number (id/1.7). Alternative per-rule form /court_rules/rule/{set}-{rule}/ (e.g. /court_rules/rule/ev-702/) also serves the text. Table of contents: /court_rules/rule/{set}-toh/ (e.g. ev-toh, cr-toh, gp-toh, aprcap-toh, prcond-toh).

automation.notes: Script is the primary route. Per-rule pages are mostly 10-35K chars including comments, but some reach ~75K (cr/id/26); WebFetch read a search-surfaced URL, while built Revisor URLs may hit PROVENANCE_REQUIRED.
